text[1]: MTEXT background fill: long[90] selects a background-fill tail shape, not a uniform on/off flag. long[90]==2 ('use drawing background color') accepts (90) alone, no further fields. Any other non-zero value (this file uses 1) gets the full (90)(63)(45)(441) tail. real[45] in that tail is a fill SCALE factor (valid ~1.0-1.5), not a height -- cell height comes from real[46].

MTEXT multi-line cells: ^J (the two literal characters caret+J, produced by Shift+Enter in AutoCAD's editor) is a soft line break within the current paragraph and responds cleanly to \H height scaling. \P (plain Enter) starts a new paragraph governed by AutoCAD's 'Paragraph Line Spacing' model, which resists tight vertical compression. ^J is what makes the 3-line number/symbol/name layout fit a fixed-height cell. \pxa0.25,se0.4; (an inline serialization of the documented Paragraph dialog Space Before/After feature -- see https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2027/ENU/?guid=GUID-90F5A530-BB66-4264-86F0-D5F670EC8519 ) is a secondary refinement layered on top of ^J, not load-bearing by itself.
MTEXT cell geometry: 10x10 unit cells, insertion point at cell CENTER, middle-center attachment (int[71]=5). real[44]=0.35 (tightened line spacing) fits three lines without overflow.

long text overflow: Element names up to 13 chars (e.g. Rutherfordium) can overflow a 10-unit cell width at full scale. \W<factor>; applied once name length exceeds 11 chars, scaling continuously rather than a hard cutoff, so longer names compress gracefully instead of wrapping or truncating.
coordinate convention: Bottom-left origin, Y increasing upward, all-positive x/y for the main grid; legend and note-like content sit in -y.
